solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 12 awkwardly holding cut beast

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the jumbled letters go around the next piece
something done awkwardly is clumsy and out of order, so the letters of the cross-referenced answer are jumbled

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily grips a slaughtered animal that has already been devoured.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 12 stands for the answer to 12 across, whose letters are the fodder; the cut piece sits inside the rearranged result.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a hoofed grazing animal, so it is an example of a beast.

clue.text: How a race might have started, with all speed

definitions.text: How a race might have started
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a starter once signalled the off by dropping a hat

explanation.surface: A description of how a race began, and quickly at that.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally describes an informal race start signalled by a falling hat, and idiomatically means instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means doing something instantly with no hesitation, which is acting with all speed.

clue.text: Care for something special

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give medical attention to
second meaning: a special pleasure or indulgence

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about looking after something precious, but splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor will treat a patient, caring for them; a treat is also a special indulgence or delight.

clue.text: Pub owner, perhaps, seen distressed by horrible insects

indicators.note: distressed means battered or roughed up, so the letters of the word beside it are knocked out of shape

parts.note: lice are parasitic insects most people find horrible

explanation.surface: A landlord was seen upset by a plague of nasty bugs in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read in reverse clue order: LICE comes first, then the jumbled SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensee holds the licence to sell alcohol, so a pub landlord is a typical example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Head of Property managed end of housing crash

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: The head of a property firm oversaw the collapse of the housing market.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor crash, especially of a car or aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is informal British for a collision or accident involving a vehicle, a synonym of crash.

clue.text: Fixed cause of poor reception

definitions.meaning: second meaning: crackling electrical interference on a radio

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' looks like 'repaired', as if the reception problem was solved, but it means motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means not moving, and static is also atmospheric interference that spoils radio or television signals.

clue.text: Navigator takes volunteers to southern isle

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A seafarer carries volunteer crew to an island in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Abel Tasman was the Dutch explorer who reached Tasmania and New Zealand; the southern isle in the surface hints at Tasmania.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was a seventeenth-century Dutch seafaring explorer, an example of a navigator.

clue.text: Ruin a garment, beginning to tear in fury?

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck it, so the letters are broken up and remade
the beginning of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a piece of clothing, ripping it in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, overbearing woman, as is a fury in the old figurative sense of an avenging spirit.

clue.text: Edit extremely early Burt Lancaster work

indicators.note: editing reworks a text, so all these letters are rearranged
the extremes of a word are its two end letters

explanation.surface: A film editor cuts an early Burt Lancaster movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor's name looks like the subject, but his letters plus the ends of 'early' are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canterbury Tales is Chaucer's collection of stories, a literary work.

clue.text: The usual flag

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the normal or default
second meaning: a banner, as carried in battle

explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal or customary, and a standard is also a military banner or ensign.

clue.text: Cutting ditch with worker

parts.note: a trench is a long ditch
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A labourer digging a ditch alongside a workmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like the act of digging the ditch; it is the adjective meaning incisive.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant remarks are sharp and incisive, a figurative synonym of cutting.

clue.text: Father Brown finally married a temptress

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a male parent

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Chesterton's priest-detective Father Brown at last weds a seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Brown is G. K. Chesterton's clerical detective; the name splits into two separate pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Sirens lured sailors with song, so a siren is a seductive, dangerous woman.

clue.text: It's said school for the rich scoffed

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the school

parts.note: Eton College is an expensive English private school

explanation.surface: People say a school for wealthy children has been mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' seems to mean jeered at, but in British slang it also means gobbled up.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is British informal for eating it greedily, so scoffed is a synonym.

clue.text: Engine put outside a drinking den

parts.note: a gin is a machine, as in the cotton gin

indicators.note: one word placed outside another wraps around it

explanation.surface: An engine is installed outside a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside PLACE after its first letter, giving PALACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin palace was a gaudy Victorian pub, so it is a showy drinking establishment.

clue.text: Athlete on mountain eating a vegetable

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside

parts.note: ben is Scottish for a mountain

explanation.surface: A runner on a mountain snacks on some veg.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner bean is a climbing plant grown for its long edible pods, an example of a vegetable.

clue.text: They're tiny and barely matter

parts.note: surface reading: small and unimportant things
setter's reading: subatomic particles of almost no mass that scarcely interact with matter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely matter' sounds dismissive, but it is literal physics: these particles are almost massless and pass through ordinary matter.
explanation.definitionFit: These subatomic particles have almost zero mass and rarely interact with matter, which is the physics behind the phrase.

clue.text: Diligent student's grub

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an insect larva that bores into books

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food the student eats, but it is a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen reader is called this, and literally it names a beetle larva that tunnels through book bindings.

clue.text: Talk idly about rare clothes

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for rare

explanation.surface: Gossiping about unusual outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothing or dress, often of a distinctive kind.

clue.text: Get painting from tall building right away!

indicators.note: sending something away removes it from the word

explanation.surface: An order to grab a picture out of a high-rise at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Rs are removed from SKYSCRAPER, leaving SKYSCAPE; 'right away!' also reads as 'immediately'.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyscape is a picture whose subject is the sky, as a landscape depicts land.

clue.text: Dog swallows large piece of tobacco

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog gulps down a big chunk of tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a compressed cake of chewing tobacco, or a bite cut from one.

clue.text: Bug makes 1000 notepads run poorly

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: K, for kilo, stands for a thousand
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An insect produces a thousand notebooks that sell badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' is used in its strict sense of a true bug, an insect order that includes this water-surface skater.
explanation.definitionFit: The pond skater is a long-legged insect of the order Hemiptera, the true bugs, that glides over water.

clue.text: Old head swallows one drug to help rest

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside

parts.note: the pate is the top of the head

explanation.surface: An elderly person takes a pill to help them sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: O stands before PATE, which takes I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic derived from opium that dulls pain and induces sleep.

clue.text: If returning oarsman holds record it shows strength

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: something that holds another keeps it inside

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: If a rower coming back holds a record, that proves strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' tempts as a sporting best for the oarsman, but here it is the old vinyl format.
explanation.definitionFit: Firepower is the destructive capacity of weapons, hence figuratively military or general strength.

clue.text: Official carries note to do with organs

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within

parts.note: real in the sense of genuine, authorised
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A functionary carries a memo about bodily organs.
explanation.walkthrough: N sits inside REAL after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, which are organs of the body.

clue.text: Little container found in street

indicators.note: something found in another sits within it

explanation.surface: A small receptacle is discovered in a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' looks like an adjective for the container; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, so it describes a small amount, as little does.

clue.text: Ridge discovered by veteran returning after shelling

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read right to left
shelling strips the outer casing, so the end letters are removed

explanation.surface: An old soldier coming home from bombardment spots a mountain ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the outer V and N to leave ETERA, then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An arete is a sharp, narrow mountain ridge carved by glaciers.

clue.text: Henry meeting his rejected wife, which might have made him look red

definitions.text: which might have made him look red

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the name is turned round

parts.note: Henry VIII's fourth wife, Anne of Cleves, was rejected by him

explanation.surface: Henry VIII meets the wife he spurned, and his face might have reddened.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII divorced Anne of Cleves soon after meeting her; ANNE written backwards gives NNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye from a plant, used to colour hair and skin red.

clue.text: A campanologist might seem familiar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a bell-ringer literally does
second meaning: the idiom for jogging the memory

explanation.walkthrough: A campanologist is a bell-ringer; the idiom also means to sound familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: When something sounds vaguely familiar we say it rings a bell, and a bell-ringer literally does so.

clue.text: Tenor requested to be given something to do

explanation.surface: A singer is asked to take on a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tasked is to be assigned a duty or job to carry out.

clue.text: Having no idea what I want to do after retirement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ignorant, without a clue

definitions.text: what I want to do after retirement
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as two words, what a crossword setter hopes to do

explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' is the setter, who in retirement would write fewer clues, so CLUE LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Clueless means ignorant or without a clue; split up, the letters describe a setter writing fewer clues.
